{
  "project_id": "P-PAK-ResilientAccessibleMicrofinance",
  "risks": [
    {
      "risk_id": "R01",
      "description": "Severe floods could trigger a sharp rise in non‑performing loans and erode capital adequacy of micro‑finance banks, limiting their lending capacity.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 5,
      "mitigation": "Activate the Contingent Liquidity Facility promptly, maintain capital buffers, and monitor NPL trends to provide early liquidity support.",
      "evidence": "Floods 2022 caused NPLs to surge 25.7% and CAR to fall from 14.9% to 11.7%, impairing sector lending."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R02",
      "description": "The Climate Risk Fund may be under‑capitalised to meet funding needs of large or extreme flood events.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Conduct annual financial modelling, secure additional capital or insurance back‑stop, and obtain Board approval for any extra funding.",
      "evidence": "CRF capitalised at US$125 m; expansion of coverage to additional climate risks would require additional capital subject to approval."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R03",
      "description": "Delays in activating CRF triggers due to slow government emergency declarations or data gaps could postpone liquidity disbursement.",
      "category": "schedule",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Define pre‑agreed quantitative thresholds, automate data feeds from third‑party providers, and establish clear SOPs for trigger verification.",
      "evidence": "Triggers require government emergency declaration or portfolio impact thresholds, with data supplied by third‑party service providers."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R04",
      "description": "Governance conflicts or mismanagement within the Trust structure could compromise CRF operations.",
      "category": "organizational",
      "likelihood": 2,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Implement an Oversight Committee, conduct independent internal and external audits, and enforce fiduciary safeguards in the Trust Deed.",
      "evidence": "CRF established as a Trust owned by GoP, managed by SBP as Trustee; Oversight and Working Committees will govern operations."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R05",
      "description": "Non‑compliance with legal covenants (e.g., unauthorized amendment of the Trust Deed) could lead to project suspension.",
      "category": "political_regulatory",
      "likelihood": 2,
      "impact": 5,
      "mitigation": "Perform regular legal compliance reviews, obtain prior written consent for any amendment, and maintain legal counsel oversight.",
      "evidence": "Legal covenants require Trust Deed not be amended without Association consent and specify obligations for SBP."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R06",
      "description": "Risk modelling currently excludes droughts, extreme heat and other hazards, potentially under‑estimating sector exposure.",
      "category": "technical",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Expand modelling to incorporate additional climate hazards and update trigger parameters accordingly.",
      "evidence": "Preliminary risk modelling limited to floods; future work will consider extreme heat and droughts."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R07",
      "description": "Increased agritech financing may lead to higher use of fertilizers and pesticides, causing localized environmental degradation.",
      "category": "environmental",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Integrate environmental safeguards, promote integrated pest management, and monitor chemical usage in loan‑linked agritech projects.",
      "evidence": "Cumulative impacts may increase fertilizer, pesticide use and air/soil pollution in loan‑clustered areas."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R08",
      "description": "Women borrowers may receive less than the targeted share of CRF liquidity, limiting gender‑inclusive resilience gains.",
      "category": "stakeholder",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Enforce the 55% women beneficiary target, impose higher borrowing costs for non‑compliance, and provide gender‑sensitive training for loan officers.",
      "evidence": "Project aims for at least 55% women beneficiaries; higher borrowing cost if deviation occurs."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R09",
      "description": "Macroeconomic instability could reduce borrowers’ repayment capacity, increasing default risk after floods.",
      "category": "external",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Design flexible loan terms, monitor macro indicators, and adjust liquidity provision to support stressed borrowers.",
      "evidence": "Macro‑economic crisis since 2019 amplified flood impacts, leading to higher NPLs and reduced sector growth."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R10",
      "description": "Failure to secure the parametric insurance back‑stop would leave the CRF under‑funded for extreme events.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 2,
      "impact": 5,
      "mitigation": "Conduct annual financial and technical reviews of the insurance product, maintain a reserve fund, and explore alternative reinsurance options.",
      "evidence": "Insurance back‑stop purchase decided annually; premium funded by GSFF grant and CRF investment income."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R11",
      "description": "Delays in establishing the CRF Trust and capitalising it could postpone project start‑up and liquidity provision.",
      "category": "schedule",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Set clear milestones for Trust registration, front‑load funding to pooled accounts, and monitor progress with monthly reporting.",
      "evidence": "Funds will be front‑loaded to pooled account for CRF capitalization; trust structure requires registration."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R12",
      "description": "Poor quality or untimely MIS data may impair monitoring, trigger decisions and overall project performance.",
      "category": "technical",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Strengthen MIS infrastructure, conduct regular data quality audits, and provide capacity‑building for SBP staff.",
      "evidence": "SBP responsible for MIS; data sources include bi‑annual reviews, financial audit, MIS, beneficiary surveys."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R13",
      "description": "Insufficient citizen engagement could result in loan products that do not match beneficiary needs, reducing uptake.",
      "category": "stakeholder",
      "likelihood": 2,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Deploy the real‑time interaction platform, conduct social audits, and integrate feedback into product design.",
      "evidence": "Citizen Engagement (CE) will include real‑time platform, participatory monitoring, and grievance redress mechanisms."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R14",
      "description": "Private sector may de‑risk by withdrawing lending from non‑flood‑affected areas, limiting overall financial inclusion.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Design CRF to also provide liquidity for medium‑size shocks and maintain incentives for private lenders in unaffected regions.",
      "evidence": "CRF only supports large/extreme shocks; small/medium shocks are retained by private sector."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R15",
      "description": "Agritech companies selected through AFIC may under‑perform, reducing the effectiveness of climate‑smart loans.",
      "category": "technical",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Set clear performance metrics, conduct regular audits of ATC services, and tie continued funding to demonstrated outcomes.",
      "evidence": "AFIC will select 5‑6 ATCs; loans bundled with ATC advisory support to boost yields and resilience."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R16",
      "description": "Changes in Government of Pakistan priorities or budget allocations could jeopardise long‑term CRF sustainability.",
      "category": "political_regulatory",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Secure multi‑year legislative commitments, embed CRF provisions in national finance law, and diversify funding sources.",
      "evidence": "CRF trust owned by GoP; additional financing subject to GoP and WB Board approvals."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R17",
      "description": "Insufficient private capital mobilisation despite guarantee structures may limit the scale of liquidity available to MFPs.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Align guarantee terms with market appetite, coordinate with ADB/IFC for co‑financing, and promote private sector participation through risk‑sharing incentives.",
      "evidence": "Future guarantee facility with IFC envisaged to leverage IDA resources and complement ADB de‑risking."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R18",
      "description": "Market‑based KIBOR pricing of CRF liquidity could make loans unaffordable for vulnerable borrowers, especially women.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 2,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Offer concessional rates or subsidies for women and flood‑affected borrowers, funded by the GSFF grant portion.",
      "evidence": "Market terms defined as 6‑month KIBOR; higher borrowing cost imposed if gender allocation deviates."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R19",
      "description": "Risk of fraud or misuse of CRF resources due to weak internal controls.",
      "category": "organizational",
      "likelihood": 2,
      "impact": 5,
      "mitigation": "Implement segregation of pooled and child accounts, conduct regular internal audits, and ensure external audit by Auditor General.",
      "evidence": "Internal audit department responsible for project audit; external audit by Auditor General of Pakistan."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R20",
      "description": "Parametric trigger thresholds may not reflect actual on‑ground damage, causing delayed or inappropriate payouts.",
      "category": "technical",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Use multiple data sources, calibrate triggers with historical loss data, and incorporate post‑event loss calculations for verification.",
      "evidence": "Two independent triggers: government emergency declaration or portfolio impact; insurance back‑stop trigger based on sector‑wide portfolio loss."
    }
  ]
}

risks.description: Severe floods could trigger a sharp rise in non‑performing loans and erode capital adequacy of micro‑finance banks, limiting their lending capacity.
risks.mitigation: Activate the Contingent Liquidity Facility promptly, maintain capital buffers, and monitor NPL trends to provide early liquidity support.
risks.evidence: Floods 2022 caused NPLs to surge 25.7% and CAR to fall from 14.9% to 11.7%, impairing sector lending.

risks.description: The Climate Risk Fund may be under‑capitalised to meet funding needs of large or extreme flood events.
risks.mitigation: Conduct annual financial modelling, secure additional capital or insurance back‑stop, and obtain Board approval for any extra funding.
risks.evidence: CRF capitalised at US$125 m; expansion of coverage to additional climate risks would require additional capital subject to approval.

risks.description: Delays in activating CRF triggers due to slow government emergency declarations or data gaps could postpone liquidity disbursement.
risks.mitigation: Define pre‑agreed quantitative thresholds, automate data feeds from third‑party providers, and establish clear SOPs for trigger verification.
risks.evidence: Triggers require government emergency declaration or portfolio impact thresholds, with data supplied by third‑party service providers.

risks.description: Governance conflicts or mismanagement within the Trust structure could compromise CRF operations.
risks.mitigation: Implement an Oversight Committee, conduct independent internal and external audits, and enforce fiduciary safeguards in the Trust Deed.
risks.evidence: CRF established as a Trust owned by GoP, managed by SBP as Trustee; Oversight and Working Committees will govern operations.

risks.description: Non‑compliance with legal covenants (e.g., unauthorized amendment of the Trust Deed) could lead to project suspension.
risks.mitigation: Perform regular legal compliance reviews, obtain prior written consent for any amendment, and maintain legal counsel oversight.
risks.evidence: Legal covenants require Trust Deed not be amended without Association consent and specify obligations for SBP.

risks.description: Risk modelling currently excludes droughts, extreme heat and other hazards, potentially under‑estimating sector exposure.
risks.mitigation: Expand modelling to incorporate additional climate hazards and update trigger parameters accordingly.
risks.evidence: Preliminary risk modelling limited to floods; future work will consider extreme heat and droughts.

risks.description: Increased agritech financing may lead to higher use of fertilizers and pesticides, causing localized environmental degradation.
risks.mitigation: Integrate environmental safeguards, promote integrated pest management, and monitor chemical usage in loan‑linked agritech projects.
risks.evidence: Cumulative impacts may increase fertilizer, pesticide use and air/soil pollution in loan‑clustered areas.

risks.description: Women borrowers may receive less than the targeted share of CRF liquidity, limiting gender‑inclusive resilience gains.
risks.mitigation: Enforce the 55% women beneficiary target, impose higher borrowing costs for non‑compliance, and provide gender‑sensitive training for loan officers.
risks.evidence: Project aims for at least 55% women beneficiaries; higher borrowing cost if deviation occurs.

risks.description: Macroeconomic instability could reduce borrowers’ repayment capacity, increasing default risk after floods.
risks.mitigation: Design flexible loan terms, monitor macro indicators, and adjust liquidity provision to support stressed borrowers.
risks.evidence: Macro‑economic crisis since 2019 amplified flood impacts, leading to higher NPLs and reduced sector growth.

risks.description: Failure to secure the parametric insurance back‑stop would leave the CRF under‑funded for extreme events.
risks.mitigation: Conduct annual financial and technical reviews of the insurance product, maintain a reserve fund, and explore alternative reinsurance options.
risks.evidence: Insurance back‑stop purchase decided annually; premium funded by GSFF grant and CRF investment income.

risks.description: Delays in establishing the CRF Trust and capitalising it could postpone project start‑up and liquidity provision.
risks.mitigation: Set clear milestones for Trust registration, front‑load funding to pooled accounts, and monitor progress with monthly reporting.
risks.evidence: Funds will be front‑loaded to pooled account for CRF capitalization; trust structure requires registration.

risks.description: Poor quality or untimely MIS data may impair monitoring, trigger decisions and overall project performance.
risks.mitigation: Strengthen MIS infrastructure, conduct regular data quality audits, and provide capacity‑building for SBP staff.
risks.evidence: SBP responsible for MIS; data sources include bi‑annual reviews, financial audit, MIS, beneficiary surveys.

risks.description: Insufficient citizen engagement could result in loan products that do not match beneficiary needs, reducing uptake.
risks.mitigation: Deploy the real‑time interaction platform, conduct social audits, and integrate feedback into product design.
risks.evidence: Citizen Engagement (CE) will include real‑time platform, participatory monitoring, and grievance redress mechanisms.

risks.description: Private sector may de‑risk by withdrawing lending from non‑flood‑affected areas, limiting overall financial inclusion.
risks.mitigation: Design CRF to also provide liquidity for medium‑size shocks and maintain incentives for private lenders in unaffected regions.
risks.evidence: CRF only supports large/extreme shocks; small/medium shocks are retained by private sector.

risks.description: Agritech companies selected through AFIC may under‑perform, reducing the effectiveness of climate‑smart loans.
risks.mitigation: Set clear performance metrics, conduct regular audits of ATC services, and tie continued funding to demonstrated outcomes.
risks.evidence: AFIC will select 5‑6 ATCs; loans bundled with ATC advisory support to boost yields and resilience.

risks.description: Changes in Government of Pakistan priorities or budget allocations could jeopardise long‑term CRF sustainability.
risks.mitigation: Secure multi‑year legislative commitments, embed CRF provisions in national finance law, and diversify funding sources.
risks.evidence: CRF trust owned by GoP; additional financing subject to GoP and WB Board approvals.

risks.description: Insufficient private capital mobilisation despite guarantee structures may limit the scale of liquidity available to MFPs.
risks.mitigation: Align guarantee terms with market appetite, coordinate with ADB/IFC for co‑financing, and promote private sector participation through risk‑sharing incentives.
risks.evidence: Future guarantee facility with IFC envisaged to leverage IDA resources and complement ADB de‑risking.

risks.description: Market‑based KIBOR pricing of CRF liquidity could make loans unaffordable for vulnerable borrowers, especially women.
risks.mitigation: Offer concessional rates or subsidies for women and flood‑affected borrowers, funded by the GSFF grant portion.
risks.evidence: Market terms defined as 6‑month KIBOR; higher borrowing cost imposed if gender allocation deviates.

risks.description: Risk of fraud or misuse of CRF resources due to weak internal controls.
risks.mitigation: Implement segregation of pooled and child accounts, conduct regular internal audits, and ensure external audit by Auditor General.
risks.evidence: Internal audit department responsible for project audit; external audit by Auditor General of Pakistan.
